items.html:
Colombian licence plates are typically yellow.

NOTE: Within South America, yellow licence plates are almost exclusively found in Colombia.

In Generation 3 coverage, a short thick antenna is sometimes visible with a black, white or grey car. In Generation 4 coverage, a white or silver car is commonly found.

NOTE: Within the Americas, you can also find the antenna in Mexico, Ecuador and Brazil. However, Colombia is the only country with this antenna on a black Google car.

Signposts in Colombia are made of white metal, and join to form a distinct cross on the back of signs.

NOTE: White metal signposts can also be found in Brazil, however these are usually wider.

Colombia uses two types of kilometre markers: a tall green version with the letters “Pr” at the top, and the traditional stone marker with black lettering. Both designs are unique to the country.

NOTE: The first two digits at the bottom indicate the road number. In this case, the road number is 90. The last two digits indicate the section of the road, which increase west to east on even numbered highways, and south to north on odd numbered highways.You can use this resource to help identify each section.
Colombian poles are often marked with unique black-and-yellow or black-and-orange stripes.

Wooden fences are particularly common in Colombia.

NOTE: In addition to the unpainted variants, some fence posts are painted and sharp at the top. These are almost exclusive to Colombia.

Colombian taxis are always this pastel yellow colour. As opposed to private vehicles, they have white licence plates, which are often printed on the side and roof. If unblurred, you will often see the city name.

NOTE: Ecuadorian taxis may look similar. However, they use a slightly more saturated yellow and typically have orange plates.

Colombian poles are generally concrete with a variety of pole tops.

Moreover, dark-coloured poles are more common in Colombia than in neighbouring countries.

NOTE: It is the only country in the Americas, apart from Mexico and Ecuador, where octagonal poles can be found.
In Colombia, it is particularly common for sidewalks to be decorated with reddish tiles.
Coverage in Colombia is mainly found in the north and west. The islands of Providencia and San Andrés, northwest of the mainland, also have coverage.
The Northern part of the country is characterised by white, sandy soil and an arid landscape.
East of the Andes lies a vast lowland called Llanos. It is characterised by open tropical grasslands, savannas with scattered trees, small areas of forest and seasonal flooding.

These pole markings with one short black strip on the top and bottom, and a longer yellow section in the middle, are most commonly found in the Antioquia department. Sometimes, you can find them in the Cordoba department as well.
As a result of slave trade, the Pacific coast of Colombia is home to an overwhelming majority of Afro-Colombians.
Sugar cane is grown along the Cauca river in Valle del Cauca and neighbouring departments.
A camera glitch that makes a part of the image look very saturated can be found in southern Colombia.

This landscape is typical of the far Northern province of La Guajira: extreme dryness, low vegetation and occasional cacti.

In addition, you can often recognise the Uribia-Puerto Bolivar road because of this landscape, the straightness and the train track always present to the East.

You can recognise the narrow Ruta 90 landbridge between Barranquilla and Cienaga thanks to the dashed yellow lines and shallow bodies of water next to the road. Open ocean can often be seen to the north.

NOTE: In the older Generation 3 coverage, you will also see tall mountains in the distance.

Intersections in the coastal city of Barranquilla are commonly marked by small concrete poles (_mojones_) bearing street names. For example, this image was taken at the intersection of Carrera 42 and Calle 68.

This unique vehicle can be found in and around Leticia, the Southernmost town in Colombia.

NOTE: The long concrete blocks seen in the bottom left corner are a reliable way of recognising the road North of Leticia.
Coverage on the Caribbean island of San Andrés was taken by this distinct white car.
The island of Providencia, located roughly 90 kilometres North of San Andrés, is home to this unique grey truck.

Providencia street lights are green and supported by a trapezoidal sheet of metal underneath.

NOTE: The uniquely shaped supporting metal piece can also be found in Barranquilla.

steps.html:
In addition, here are some resources to help you practise Colombia:

  • Plonk It Colombia (map link) - This map contains locations for practising each meta in the Plonk It Colombia guide from step 2 to 3.

lm.name: Colombia
lm.note:
Colombian licence plates are typically yellow.

NOTE: Within South America, yellow licence plates are almost exclusively found in Colombia.

lm.name: Agriculture - Aracataca Cut Palms
lm.note: These palms where the crown has been cut, are very often found near Aracataca and some smaller towns North of it.

lm.name: Agriculture - Banana
lm.note: In general, banana plantation can be found mostly in Quindio and Magdalena, sometimes in Northwest-Antioquia and Cordoba, and rarely in surrounding provinces of Quindio.

lm.name: Agriculture - Banana - Cloudy Gen 3
lm.note:
Large amounts of banana plants in plantations are commonly found in different areas.

Paired with Cloudy Gen 3 Coverage, they're most common in Northwestern Antioquia.

lm.name: Agriculture - Banana - Dry
lm.note: In Magdalena you will often see banana plantations in a dry sandy/dirty area with mountains to your east.

lm.name: Agriculture - Banana - Hedge
lm.note: In Quindio you will commonly find banana plantations behind hedges.

lm.name: Agriculture - Banana - Small Field / No Hedge
lm.note: In the states surrounding Quindio you will find smaller banana plantations along the road not behind hedges.

lm.name: Agriculture - Coffee
lm.note:
The coffee belt stretches in the valley between Medellin and Cali. In the North, you will only find it near the Venezuelan border.

Olives and Tea have a very similar distribution.

lm.name: Agriculture - Common Guava
lm.note: Common Guava mostly appears in the valley between the western and the central mountain range in Colombia, but it can also appear in other valleys.

lm.name: Agriculture - Guadua Bamboo
lm.note: Guadua Bamboo plantations are found mainly in Caldas, but also in the adjecent Tolima, Quindio and Risaralda.

lm.name: Agriculture - Oil Palms
lm.note: Oilpalms can be found mainly in Meta and Casanare. They are also very common around the 45 near Fundacion and Aracataca. Sometimes, you can find them in Barrancabermeja.

lm.name: Agriculture - Sugarcane
lm.note: Sugarcane will mainly be found in Cauca and Valle de Cauca.

lm.name: Architecture - Guatape
lm.note: Bright Colored Houses & Unique Pavement.

lm.name: Architecture - Straw/Thatched Roofs
lm.note: Houses with roofs like this are commonly found along the coast, especially near Cartagena and Barranquilla.

lm.name: Car Meta - Gen 3 - white/blue striped car
lm.note: Gen 3 with the white-blue car follows a straight line between Cartagena and Medellín, has partial coverage along Route 80 west of Bosconia, as well as along Route 45 north of Bucaramanga and east of Medellín.

lm.name: Car Meta - Gen 4 - Grey Car
lm.note: Gen 4 coverage with the grey car is not found north of Montería, has a gap between Bucaramanga and Bogotá, forms a 'staircase' pattern with right angles at Medellín and Bogotá, covers areas around Bucaramanga, and has a missing section around Popayán.

lm.name: Car Meta - Gen 4 - White Car
lm.note: Gen 4 with the white car has no coverage south of Cali, very little around Medellín, and forms a curved pattern around Medellín.

lm.name: Car Meta - Leticia
lm.note:
This unique vehicle can be found in and around Leticia, the Southernmost town in Colombia.

NOTE: The long concrete blocks seen in the bottom left corner are a reliable way of recognising the road North of Leticia.

lm.name: Car Meta - Providencia
lm.note: The island of Providencia, located roughly 90 kilometres North of San Andrés, is home to this unique grey truck.

lm.name: Car Meta - San Andres
lm.note: Coverage on the Caribbean island of San Andrés was taken by this distinct white car.

lm.name: Coverage Meta - "Gen 5" Glitch
lm.note: A camera glitch that makes a part of the image look very saturated can be found in southern Colombia.

lm.name: Coverage Meta - Arauca Rift
lm.note: On the road in Arauca and in the city of Arauca in northeastern Colombia, there is virtually only cloudy, bad weather coverage. Furthermore, there was a small camera glitch where you can see this small rift northeast of the driving direction.

lm.name: Coverage Meta - Double Google Car
lm.note: A Second Google Car is visible in many random spots. The most prominent spots are the 26 in Cauca, Vda. Chontaduro (near Popoyan) and the road between Pital and Tarqui.

lm.name: Coverage Meta - Double Google Car - Aguachica
lm.note: This instance of a second google car can be seen on Carrera 4, an offroad of the 45 near Aguachica.

lm.name: Coverage Meta - Double Google Car - Villavicencio
lm.note: This instance of a second google car can be seen on the east-west road, directly south of Guayuriba River, which is south of Villavicencio.

lm.name: Coverage Meta - Embalse Calima
lm.note: Large lake, mostly winter coverage. A small stretch also has summer coverage.

lm.name: Coverage Meta - Foggy & Rainy Coverage
lm.note: If you see rainy coverage, combined with strong fog, you're on the 64.

lm.name: Coverage Meta - Grey Car, 2023 copyright
lm.note: This constellation can be found on the 65 in Caqueta and the 45 in Putumayo.

lm.name: Coverage Meta - La Florida
lm.note: Rainy coverage with very orange-brown soil can be found on this road to La Florida.

lm.name: Coverage Meta - Rainy Coverage
lm.note: Rainy coverage is most common on the highways 20, 24, 50 and 64.

lm.name: Coverage Meta - Sogamoso Lake
lm.note: If you see a lake, paired with an overexposed Gen 4 camera, you're probably on this lake south of Sogamoso.

lm.name: Coverage Meta - Stick Meta
lm.note: This stick on the camera can be found between El Guio and El Boral (near the Cundinamarca-Meta border near Villavicencio)

lm.name: Coverage Meta - Unique Road - Tame to Arauca
lm.note: On this road, you can see a sunset through the clouds. It's not always easy to recognize, however.

lm.name: Coverage Meta - Unique Road - Tame to Hato Corozal
lm.note: On this road, you can see a slight sunset through the clouds. It is pretty flat, with mountains in the Northwest.

lm.name: Infrastructure - Barichara Pavement
lm.note: This unique cobblestone pavement is found is the historic town of Barichara, Santander.

lm.name: Infrastructure - Barranquilla Roadbollard
lm.note: In Barranquilla, you can often find this bollard with roadnames on intersections.

lm.name: Infrastructure - Buenaventura Truck Spam Road
lm.note: The stretch of the 40 to Buenaventura is an important route for trucks, so if you see many trucks, it's worth a thought.

lm.name: Infrastructure - Caldas Polepaint
lm.note: orange & blue

lm.name: Infrastructure - Cauca/Narino Polepaint
lm.note: Yellow with dark numbers

lm.name: Infrastructure - Coastal Antioquia Polepaint
lm.note: Green paint with yellow numbers

lm.name: Infrastructure - Electricity Counter - Oval
lm.note:
Usually pretty tall with oval windows, circle windows might not be as trustworthy.

Very common as there are few plastic counters in this region.

lm.name: Infrastructure - European Bollard
lm.note: This european-style (specifically spanish style bollard) is found in Cundinamarca, but also on the 40 towards Villavicencio.

lm.name: Infrastructure - H-shaped lamp attachment
lm.note: H-shaped lamp attachment plates can be found in Bogota.

lm.name: Infrastructure - Huila Polepaint
lm.note: Orange paint with black numbers

lm.name: Infrastructure - Ibague Lamp
lm.note:
This red lamp style is unique to Tolima province.

Note by MB: I only found it in Ibague, not in any other towns in Tolima. Also, the meta is more about the color and the shape of the lamp, not about the arrangement of the lights.

lm.name: Infrastructure - Megabus
lm.note: Green or yellow, modern bus. Often on a dedicated bus lane. Found in Pereira metropolitan area.

lm.name: Infrastructure - Pole Marking - Antioquia
lm.note: These pole markings with one short black strip on the top and bottom, and a longer yellow section in the middle, are most commonly found in the Antioquia department. Sometimes, you can find them in the Cordoba department as well.

lm.name: Infrastructure - QR-Code Sticker
lm.note: Found in Barranquilla and Santa Marta

lm.name: Infrastructure - Rectangular lamp attachment
lm.note: Rectangular lamp attachment plates can be found mainly in Medellin, sometimes further North, especially in Monteria and Cucuta.

lm.name: Infrastructure - Risaralda/Choco Polepaint
lm.note: Yellow paint with red numbers. Found all over Risaralda and the towns of Istmina and Quibdo in Choco.

lm.name: Infrastructure - Sarawak Pole
lm.note: Asymmetrical poles with a "Sarawak" extension (a vertical stalk coming out the top), can often be found East of Andes. Note that this pole is not 100%, and has been spotted elsewhere.

lm.name: Infrastructure - Spikes
lm.note: These spikes can be found on the 40 and the 62.

lm.name: Infrastructure - Street Lamps - Barranquilla
lm.note: The uniquely shaped supporting metal piece can be found in Barranquilla. (Similar to the Providencia design)

lm.name: Infrastructure - Street Lamps - Providencia
lm.note: Providencia street lights are green and supported by a trapezoidal sheet of metal underneath. (The metal sheet without a green lamp can also be found in Barranquilla)

lm.name: Infrastructure - Tinto Bus
lm.note: This red bus drives in the town (not the country) Armenia.

lm.name: Infrastructure - Tolima Poletag
lm.note: Orange tag with white numbers

lm.name: Infrastructure - TransLago vans
lm.note: TransLogo vans are common throughtout Boyaca Department. You will most often see them on the routes Tunja-Sogamoso and Tunja-Duitama.

lm.name: Infrastructure - Transmetro
lm.note: White Transmetro buses can be found in Barranquilla.

lm.name: Infrastructure - Tumaco
lm.note: If you see many puddles and a pavement out of '+' shaped stones, you're in Tumaco.

lm.name: Infrastructure - Valle de Cauca Pole
lm.note: If you see these poletops you will find yourself in Valle Del Cauca.

lm.name: Infrastructure - Valle de Cauca Polepaint
lm.note: Yellow, with black numbers. Several digits can be in one row.

lm.name: Infrastructure - Villavicencio Bike Lane Road
lm.note: If you see a bike lane, and get East of Andes vibes, you're most likely on the road through Los Tobitos to Villavicencio.

lm.name: Landscape - Deep grey & stony soil in Gen 3
lm.note: This type of soil can be found in towns near the pacific coast.

lm.name: Landscape - East of Andes Landscape
lm.note:
East of the Andes lies a vast lowland called Llanos. It is characterised by open tropical grasslands, savannas with scattered trees, small areas of forest and seasonal flooding.

Since it's to the east of the Andes, you may see mountains in the west, but never in the east.

lm.name: Landscape - Guatape Hill
lm.note: This striking cone-shaped mountain can often be seen from the surrounding area of Guatape.

lm.name: Landscape - Guaviare Orange Road
lm.note: The only road in Guaviare goes from to Guaviare (city), and continues south up until Vda. El Trueno. It can be recognized by the orange-looking dust on the road.

lm.name: Landscape - La Guajira
lm.note: This landscape is typical of the far Northern province of La Guajira: extreme dryness, low vegetation and occasional cacti.

lm.name: Landscape - Northern Landscape
lm.note: The Northern part of the country is characterised by white, sandy soil and an arid landscape.

lm.name: Landscape - Paramos
lm.note:
Paramos refers to alpine tundra ecosystems located in the mountains. These kinds of regions are easy to guess by how little vegetation grows here. The best clue is these odd looking pants. ( giant rosette plants ).

Note by MB: In my experience, this appears most commonly south of Bogota, still in the capital district.

lm.name: Landscape - Pasto Hills
lm.note:
In southern Colombia, around the city of Pasto, there are hilly fields that are unique in that they are bordered by hedges. The hedges are very thick and form very distinctive lines on the hills. It almost gives off a “British” vibe. If you are sure that it is Colombia, this is a very good meta, but such fields with hedges also occur in Ecuador.

!! In very rare cases, such hedges on hills can also occur in other parts of Colombia. !!

lm.name: Landscape - Santa Rosalia
lm.note: Santa Rosalia is the only town covered in Vichada. So if you see red/orange dirt in an urban Gen 4 loc, you should go there.

lm.name: Landscape - Swamp Road + Extremely Sunny
lm.note: If you see a swamp road with extremely sunny coverage, you're probably on the 74 in Sucre.

lm.name: Landscape - Swamp Roads
lm.note: The 74, the 78 and a few other roads more north have very swampy parts, you can see on the map where these are by zooming.

lm.name: Landscape - Unique Road - 78 west of Pailitas
lm.note: This road is characterised by low clouds and a towering mountain in the east.

lm.name: Landscape - Unique Road - Ruta 90 Landbridge
lm.note:
You can recognise the narrow Ruta 90 landbridge between Barranquilla and Cienaga thanks to the dashed yellow lines and shallow bodies of water next to the road. Open ocean can often be seen to the north.

NOTE: In the older Generation 3 coverage, you will also see tall mountains in the distance.

lm.name: Landscape - Unique Road - Uribia to Puerto Boliviar
lm.note: You can often recognise the Uribia-Puerto Bolivar road because of La Guajira landscape (extreme dryness, low vegetation and occasional cacti), the straightness and the train track always present to the East.

lm.name: Landscape - Vichada Red Dirt
lm.note: Vichada is characterize by hazy Gen 4 coverage and Red Dirt.

lm.name: Misc - Afro-Colombians
lm.note: As a result of slave trade, the Pacific coast of Colombia is home to an overwhelming majority of Afro-Colombians.

lm.name: Trekker - Trebal Resort Trekker
lm.note: This trekker can be recognized by the unique pavement and houses.

lm.name: Vegetation - Cacti
lm.note: Cacti are most commonly found in the North near Valledupar. Sometimes they can appear in Huila, too.

lm.name: Vegetation - Colombian Mahogany
lm.note: This tree is found mainly around Medellin, but it has been spotted in other random spots.

lm.name: Vegetation - Kapok Tree
lm.note: The Kapok tree can be found throughout Colombia, but is most common between the central and eastern mountain range.

lm.name: Vegetation - Quindio Wax Palm
lm.note: This palm is found in mountainous regions of Colombia, mainly in Quindio, as the name suggests.

lm.name: Vegetation - Veracruz Trees
lm.note: In Colombia you will most commonly find these trees that appear to have a knot on top of their trunk in the dark red areas. The province of Cordoba has the most gen 4 out of the others so if you see these in gen 4 consider Cordoba. (If the area is flat/semi hilly, You can find these trees in the mountains aswell everywhere)

lm.name: Vegetation - Wide Trees
lm.note: These wide trees, usually near fences, are found in Northern regions, especially near Monteria and Sincelejo.

lm.name: Colombian cross
lm.note:
Signposts in Colombia are made of white thin metal and have a distinct cross on the back.

In the photo, green checkmarks show the "real" Colombian cross, and red X's show the ones that aren't right.

lm.name: Yellow plates
lm.note:
In South America, yellow license plates are almost exclusive to Colombia. Commercial vehicles in Colombia may have white plates.

lm.name: Isla de Providencia car
lm.note: On the tiny Isla de Providencia, Google used a small silver truck with a long antenna

lm.name: Max north Colombia vibes
lm.note: The northern tip of Colombia looks a lot like Tumbes and Piura in Peru, but with more cacti and a different car

lm.name: San Andrés car
lm.note: On the small island of San Andrés, Google used a small white truck with no antenna

lm.name: Agriculture - Common Guava
lm.note: Common Guava mostly appears in the valley between the western and the central mountain range in Colombia, but it can also appear in other valleys.

lm.name: Landscape - Orocue Road
lm.note: This road leading from the 65 to the town of Orocue is characterized by its unique angle and the orange/brown dirt.

lm.name: Vegetation - Colombian Mahogany
lm.note: This tree is found mainly around Medellin, but it has been spotted in other random spots.

lm.name: Vegetation - Quindio Wax Palm
lm.note: This palm is found in mountainous regions of Colombia, mainly in Quindio, as the name suggests.

lm.name: 2023 - 2023 copyright with grey Google car
lm.note: Grey google car with 2023 copyright can often be found on the 65 & 45 in Putumayo & Caqueta

lm.name: 2024  - 2024 copyright on the 10 towards Tumaco
lm.note: This road is fully 2024 with the off road towards Candelilas as well

lm.name: 2024  - 2024 copyright on the 40
lm.note: This road got almost full 2024 coverage now with red/orange dirt getting more orange the more east you go

lm.name: 40 unique highway - 40 unique highway
lm.note:
This highway going from Bogota to Villavicencio is unique due to the 2 overlapping highways going in and out of tunnels with spikes on the side, the 62 above medellin also has alot of spikes but the 40 also has bollards.

So if you got a divided highway through the andes with potential bollards & spikes + tunnels, good chance you're on this road!

lm.name: 5 black dots in the sky - 5 black dots in the sky
lm.note: On this road east of Neiva you find old january 2014 coverage with 5-7 black dots in the sky, there is a little bit of this coverage in Neiva as well but most of it is overwritten so this road is your best guess.

lm.name: 65 Hato - 65 Hato
lm.note: The 64 is an unique road going through the andes with alot of rain coverage, you end up on this 65 road to the east with significant unique mountains to the north/west.

lm.name: 90 north - 90 north
lm.note: May 2024 coverage on the 90 east to west on the north coast, Ocean north and Pico Cristobal Colon to the east, look out for the silhouette of Pico Cristobal Colon.

lm.name: Antioquia Sticker - Antioquia Sticker
lm.note: In Northwestern Antioquia you can find these green and yellow pole markings, you can find them in southern Antioquia but they are much less common.

lm.name: Atlantico - Atlantico looks similar to Bolivar, Sucre, Cordoba but with slightly more hills at times. Veracruz trees with alot of gen3 on rural roads
Avella - Trans Avella
lm.note: Trans Avella S.A. is a transportation company operating within Colombia, specifically in the Boyacá department. They offer intermunicipal bus services connecting various cities and towns within the region. Popular Routes: Tunja to Sogamoso Tunja to Duitama

lm.name: bamboo - Bamboo
lm.note: The Colombian departments (states) with the highest woody bamboo diversity are Norte de Santander, Cundinamarca, Cauca, Valle del Cauca, Antioquia, Huila, Nariño and Quindío.. There are massive plantations in Quindio, these are covered mostly in old december 2014 coverage.

lm.name: Baranquilla Lamps - Barranquilla unique lamp
lm.note: These lamps are in the city of Barranquilla

lm.name: Baranquilla QR Sticker - Baranquilla QR Sticker
lm.note: This sticker with a QR code is found in Baranquilla, Riohacha also uses the same sticker.

lm.name: Barichara Pavement - Barichara Pavement
lm.note: This unique cobblestone pavement is found is the historic town of Barichara, Santander.

lm.name: Bike lane Girardot - Bike Lane west of Girardot
lm.note: This bike lane is quite long and good chance you can get it in a duel, good to know and easy to pinpoint with the road angle!

lm.name: Bike Lane Sincelejo  - Bike Lane Sincelejo - Corozal
lm.note: This coverage was taken sept 2024, it's a nice green road and in the northern bits of colombia you find almost no bike lanes outside the cities

lm.name: Bike lane Villavicencio  - Bike lane Villavicencio - 65
lm.note: Another bike lane coming out of Villavicencio, I find this one usefull since I sometimes struggle with urban east of andes locations like Villavicencio & Yopal so good to know. These overpasses are also common around cities like Bogota, Cali or Medellin popular pedestrian walkable areas but they can be found anywhere where they need one in big cities.

lm.name: Bike Lane Villavicencio - Bike Lane Villavicencio
lm.note: This bike lane is on a north/south road with east of andes vibes

lm.name: Black & White sticker - Black & White sticker in Cali (Valle De Cauca)
lm.note: Black & White sticker in Cali (Valle De Cauca)

lm.name: Black car 2023 copyright - Grey car 2023 copyright
lm.note: Oktober 2022 copyright but uploaded in 2023 so will have 2023 copyright visible and with the grey googlecar and the landscape with a vibe you can learn by playing alot of Balanced Colombia, These roads in Putumayo and Caqueta are unique and learnable but there is ofcourse older coverage within the small towns in this province so be careful. On the main roads you will find this coverage only.

lm.name: Black Long Yellow Black - Black Long Yellow Black pole paint Antioquia province
lm.note: This pole paint can be found in Antioquia province, keep in mind this is a large province going all the way up the coast. I've also seen this paint in Cucuta so use the metal plate meta as confirmation if you can

lm.name: blue & yellow - Blue & Yellow sticker
lm.note: This sticker can be found in Cauca, Valle de Cauca

lm.name: Bocachica Guide - handsome guide
lm.note: This handsome guide follows you on the trekker in Bocachica

lm.name: Bolivar - Bolivar-Sucre-Cordoba
lm.note: In Colombia you will most commonly find these trees that appear to have a knot on top of their trunk in the dark red areas. The province of Cordoba has the most gen 4 out of the others so if you see these in gen 4 consider Cordoba. (If the area is flat/semi hilly, You can find these trees in the mountains aswell everywhere)

lm.name: Bollard - Bollard
lm.note: This spanish bollard is mostly found in Cundinamarca but also on the 40 towards Villavicencio

lm.name: Buenaventura Export
lm.note: Buenaventura road has august 2022 coverage with an east-west road angle and alot of trucks drive on this road due to it's signifance as an export city. You'll find multiple trucks on this road most of the times.

lm.name: Buenaventure Export - Buenaventura Export

top.html:
Colombian licence plates are typically yellow.

NOTE: Within South America, yellow licence plates are almost exclusively found in Colombia.
top.raw: Colombian licence plates are typically **yellow**. NOTE: Within South America, yellow licence plates are almost exclusively found in Colombia.

top.html:
In Generation 3 coverage, a short thick antenna is sometimes visible with a black, white or grey car. In Generation 4 coverage, a white or silver car is commonly found.

NOTE: Within the Americas, you can also find the antenna in Mexico, Ecuador and Brazil. However, Colombia is the only country with this antenna on a black Google car.
top.raw: In Generation 3 coverage, a **short thick antenna** is sometimes visible with a black, white or grey car. In Generation 4 coverage, a white or silver car is commonly found. NOTE: Within the Americas, you can also find the antenna in Mexico, Ecuador and Brazil. However, Colombia is the only country with this antenna on a black Google car.

top.html:
Signposts in Colombia are made of white metal, and join to form a distinct cross on the back of signs.

NOTE: White metal signposts can also be found in Brazil, however these are usually wider.
top.raw: Signposts in Colombia are made of white metal, and join to form a distinct **cross on the back** of signs. NOTE: White metal signposts can also be found in Brazil, however these are usually wider.

top.html:
Colombia uses two types of kilometre markers: a tall green version with the letters “Pr” at the top, and the traditional stone marker with black lettering. Both designs are unique to the country.

NOTE: The first two digits at the bottom indicate the road number. In this case, the road number is 90. The last two digits indicate the section of the road, which increase west to east on even numbered highways, and south to north on odd numbered highways.You can use this resource to help identify each section.
top.raw: Colombia uses two types of kilometre markers: a tall green version with the letters “**Pr**” at the top, and the traditional stone marker with black lettering. Both designs are unique to the country. NOTE: The first two digits at the bottom indicate the road number. In this case, the road number is 90. The last two digits indicate the section of the road, which increase west to east on even numbered highways, and south to north on odd numbered highways.You can use this [resource](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anexo:Carreteras_nacionales_de_Colombia) to help identify each section.

top.html: Colombian poles are often marked with unique black-and-yellow or black-and-orange stripes.
top.raw: Colombian poles are often marked with unique **black-and-yellow** or black-and-orange stripes.

top.html:
Wooden fences are particularly common in Colombia.

NOTE: In addition to the unpainted variants, some fence posts are painted and sharp at the top. These are almost exclusive to Colombia.
top.raw: **Wooden fences** are particularly common in Colombia. NOTE: In addition to the unpainted variants, some fence posts are [painted and sharp](https://maps.app.goo.gl/z7gpBcspK4rCWeep8) at the top. These are almost exclusive to Colombia.

top.html:
Colombian taxis are always this pastel yellow colour. As opposed to private vehicles, they have white licence plates, which are often printed on the side and roof. If unblurred, you will often see the city name.

NOTE: Ecuadorian taxis may look similar. However, they use a slightly more saturated yellow and typically have orange plates.
top.raw: Colombian taxis are always this **pastel yellow** colour. As opposed to private vehicles, they have white licence plates, which are often printed on the side and roof. If unblurred, you will often see the city name. NOTE: Ecuadorian taxis may look similar. However, they use a slightly more saturated yellow and typically have orange plates.

top.html:
Colombian poles are generally concrete with a variety of pole tops.

Moreover, dark-coloured poles are more common in Colombia than in neighbouring countries.

NOTE: It is the only country in the Americas, apart from Mexico and Ecuador, where octagonal poles can be found.
top.raw: Colombian poles are generally **concrete** with a variety of pole tops. Moreover, dark-coloured poles are more common in Colombia than in neighbouring countries. NOTE: It is the only country in the Americas, apart from Mexico and Ecuador, where octagonal poles can be found.

top.html: In Colombia, it is particularly common for sidewalks to be decorated with reddish tiles.
top.raw: In Colombia, it is particularly common for sidewalks to be decorated with **reddish tiles**.
